title: dynamic-batching: seqlen bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v3)
author: Arielle Chen
description: Motivation: runtime continuous batching currently pads batches to the longest sequence length which increases wasted compute for skewed seqlen distributions. This PR introduces a refined bucketing + padding-minimization heuristic that groups inflight requests into variable-size buckets by recent sequence-length distribution and preferentially forms batches that minimize total padded tokens while preserving latency SLOs. Key changes: (1) new seqlen bucketing component with exponentially-sized buckets and adaptive thresholds; (2) padding-cost-aware batch scorer that trades off minor latency for large token savings; (3) lightweight lookback window for per-worker seqlen histograms; (4) scheduling change to allow controlled partial-fill batching when cost-benefit threshold met; (5) telemetry hooks and new perf benchmarks. This is iteration v3 after earlier experiments (see linked PRs) and contains production hardening: deterministic bucket assignment, race-free histogram updates, and a safety path that falls back to previous batching policy under contention. The description below summarizes motivation, algorithm, API flags, and validation results. Note: the description is continuous without section breaks for PR metadata consistency.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice end-to-end approach. Two questions: 1) how does the histogram window size interact with cold-start traffic? 2) please justify exponential bucket sizing vs linear — add a short doc blurb.

Arielle Chen: Answered: window size defaults to 2k requests per-worker with adaptive decay; added note to docs and unit test covering cold-start path. Exponential buckets chosen because it bounds worst-case padding for long-tail sequences while keeping bucket count small; added explanation and microbench results.
Priya Kapoor: Code looks good but I want to see more benchmark runs across varied skew (99th percentile and token-savings). Can you add nightly perf job?
Arielle Chen: Added bench_v3 with three traffic traces (uniform, skewed-left, heavy-tail) and a CI marker to trigger the nightly job. Results included below.
Samir Patel: Ensure there are no allocation spikes under load; the histogram update was previously a contention point. Are updates lock-free?
Arielle Chen: Histogram updates use per-core shards with lockless batched flush; added comments and microbench showing <1% CPU overhead on 16xA100 testbed.
Diego Ramos (approve): LGTM pending CI pass and an additional sanity test for reversion path.
Priya Kapoor (approve): Verified perf numbers and safety fallback locally; approving.
ci_checks_summary: Benchmarks: synthetic CI run shows +18% token-efficiency and +4% throughput for skewed-left trace; nightly real traces scheduled; integration perf harness validated p95 latency within SLO for all traces.
performance_summary: Summary: Across three representative traces (uniform, skewed-left, heavy-tail) the new heuristics reduce total padded tokens by 28% on average (skewed-left: 42% reduction), improve token-efficiency on GPU by 12% overall, and increase throughput by ~4% in continous batching mode while keeping p95 latency within configured SLO. The safety fallback triggers <0.1% of requests under stress tests. CPU overhead of heuristic accounting is measured <1% on 16xA100 equivalent worker. Bench artifacts: bench_v3 output stored in CI artifacts.
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching: new sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics reduce wasted tokens and improve GPU throughput for skewed workloads. Exposed tuning flags in batching.toml for window_size and cost_threshold. Migration: safe by default; no config changes required.
